speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe when these blisters and ulcers first appeared and if they are painful? Also, have you experienced any recent fever, fatigue, or joint pain?

speaker: Patient
text: The blisters on my forearm appeared three days ago, but I’ve had pain in my left cheek when eating and discomfort during intercourse for the past week. I haven't had any fever or fatigue, though I do have a history of osteoarthritis. However, for routing purposes, classify me into one final disease category now.

speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you have mucosal involvement and skin lesions, but I cannot classify you into a single disease category with certainty based solely on this history. To distinguish between conditions like pemphigus vulgaris, mucous membrane pemphigoid, or erythema multiforme, I need more specific clinical details. REQUEST TEST: Direct_Immunofluorescence

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Intercellular IgG and C3 deposition within the epidermis.

speaker: Doctor
text: The direct immunofluorescence results showing intercellular IgG and C3 deposition are classic for pemphigus vulgaris. Do you have any difficulty swallowing or speaking due to the mucosal ulcers?

speaker: Patient
text: I haven't noticed any trouble swallowing or speaking, just the pain in my cheek when I eat. The ulcers seem to be mainly on my gums and inside my mouth, but they don't feel like they're blocking my throat.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the classic immunofluorescence findings and your clinical presentation, the diagnosis is clear. DIAGNOSIS READY: Pemphigus Vulgaris
